questions.stem: In an ASR→LLM→TTS pipeline, the LLM receives only the transcript and TTS receives only the generated reply text. ASR transcribes “turn right” as “turn light.” Which conclusion is warranted even if the later stages faithfully process their own inputs?
assumptions: No original audio or independent confirmation is supplied to the LLM/TTS stages; the question concerns possible propagation, not guaranteed failure on every example.

options.text: A grammatically valid LLM reply establishes that the ASR transcript preserved the intended request.
High-fidelity TTS pronunciation establishes that the original spoken command was transcribed accurately.
A mistaken word can alter the LLM’s interpreted request, and clear synthesized speech may faithfully express the resulting wrong reply.
Separately trained ASR and LLM parameters make this input error irrelevant to the LLM response.
